item.title: Further arrest in relation to the murder of Lisa Dorrian
item.description: Detectives investigating the disappearance and murder of County Down woman Lisa Dorrian, have today made a further arrest. The 25 year old was last seen alive at a caravan party in Ballyhalbert 21 years ago - and her body has never been found. A 40-year-old man's been arrested in Millisle on suspicion of assisting offenders and withholding information. Advertisement A man and woman were recently arrested on suspicion of offences including murder - but were later released on bail.

item.title: Man further remanded in relation to fatal Monaghan collision
item.description: A 56-year-old man has been further remanded in jail in relation to a fatal collision in Co Monaghan. Ion Bucurica previously appeared before Monaghan District Court in relation to dangerous driving causing the death of mother of two, Emma Mackeral. The Romanian national was last month further charged with no insurance and failure to produce in court. item.description: Gardai in Bailieboro are appealing got information following two separate burglaries. Gardai in Bailieboro are investigating a burglary which took place at the council road shed on new road, Bailieboro. item.title: Local calls to introduce new bird flu compensation scheme
item.description: A local councillor has called on the Minister for Agriculture to introduce a new compensation scheme to cover poultry farmers directly and indirectly impacted by bird flu. The motion which was brought forward by Cllr Raymond Aughey at this week’s sitting of Monaghan County Council was passed unanimously. item.title: Calls for Family Resource Centre in Cootehill
item.description: The need of a family resource centre in Cootehill was highlighted in the Seanad yesterday afternoon. A number of people from the community were present at Leinster House to highlight their calls for a resource centre in the town. Senator Joe O'Reilly called on the government to deliver the service and highlighted the positive impact that it would have on the town. item.description: In Ladies football, Cavan's derby win over Monaghan on Sunday past has put them in pole position to claim a promotion spot from Division 2. item.title: Lamb quintuplets born on Cavan farm
item.description: Quintuplet lambs have been born on a Cavan farm beating the odds of around one in a million. The O'Brien's who own and run a sheep and beef farm on the outskirts of Cavan town welcomed quintuplet lambs from one ewe last Friday night. While rare, this event occasionally occurs naturally in sheep, with survival rates for all five lambs being even lower, often described as a "one-in-a-million" occurrence. item.title: Local students launch 'Wear Again Wednesday' initiative
item.description: Secondary school pupils in Oldcastle are launching a 'Wear Again Wednesday' initiative to promote sustainable fashion. It will see students at St Oliver’s Post Primary School wear second-hand clothes to school for the day instead of their uniform. Ahead of the launch pupils hosted a swap shop where students could bring in their unwanted clothes in exchange for 'new to them' pieces brought in by their classmates. item.title: Sepsis awareness event to take place in Cavan
item.description: A sepsis awareness support evening is being held in Cavan Town tomorrow evening. North East Sepsis Awareness are hosting the event in the Hotel Kilmore from 7pm. The evening will include guest speakers and shared experiences and support surrounding the infection. item.title: Monaghan County Council wins national award
item.description: Monaghan County Council won a national award over the weekend at the 2026 LAMA All Ireland Community & Council Awards. The local authority won the Local Authority Energy Decarbonisation Award. The award recognises their Innovation in Road Maintenance project - a low carbon approach using cold mix reclaimed asphalt to strengthen the road network.
